items.followUp: State one difference between the images produced by TEM and SEM.

rubric.why: TEM transmits electrons through a thin specimen to reveal its internal structures.
rubric.description: Describes how TEM examines the specimen or what it reveals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that TEM electrons pass through a thin specimen or that TEM reveals internal structure.

rubric.why: SEM scans the specimen’s surface and produces a three-dimensional image.
rubric.description: Describes how SEM examines the specimen or the image it produces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that SEM scans the surface or produces a three-dimensional image.

modelAnswer: TEM passes electrons through a very thin specimen to show its internal structures.
SEM scans the specimen’s surface and produces a three dimensional image.

items.followUp: What is a catalyst, and what does it do to a chemical reaction?

rubric.why: Enzymes are catalysts of biological origin, produced by living cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as biological catalysts or stating that they are catalysts produced by living cells.

rubric.why: Enzymes increase the rate of reactions without being consumed.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of enzymes on reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes speed up reactions or are not consumed in the process.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst produced by living cells.
It increases the rate of a reaction and is not consumed in the process.
